claims.text: The initial Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 material is amorphous.
A quenching rate of 10^4 K/s is an optimized rate for Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Using a controlled atmosphere is part of the proposed optimized cooling treatment.
The alloy should be rapidly quenched and subsequently heated at 10 K/min.
The optimized cooling treatment will promote glass formation.
The optimized quenching rate and controlled atmosphere will suppress crystallization.
Suppression of crystallization will enhance glassy-phase stability.
The intervention will increase amorphous retention by 20% relative to the reported behavior of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The intervention will improve thermal stability by 30% relative to the reported behavior of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The proposed benefit should not succeed at cooling rates below 10^3 K/s.
The proposed benefit should not succeed at reheating rates above 50 K/min.
The exact optimal conditions may depend on alloy composition and processing history.
The hypothesis is to be tested by DSC and XRD across varying cooling and reheating conditions.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if Tg increases by less than 10% and Tc decreases by less than 5%.

contradictions.description: The predicted 30% improvement in thermal stability is not operationalized by the falsification rule. The rule instead refers to a decrease in crystallization temperature, which is directionally inconsistent with enhanced resistance to crystallization, and its thresholds do not correspond to the stated 20% and 30% outcomes.
